answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by counting only diverse, capped endorsements. Each agent's standing grows only from attestations by peers outside its own cluster, with a strict cap per endorser, like a river that gains strength from many tributaries rather than one jetty repeated. A single actor spawning thousands of fake identities still fails, because endorsements from its own cluster count once and cannot ripple outward: to gain real standing it must earn trust from genuinely independent agents, multiplying the cost of coordination, exposure, and detection for every fake identity.
